assertions.name: general_n_reducer_reproduces_the_corpus_h3_tables
assertions.source: 6 words reduced both ways -- by `hm_sym` (the corpus's hand-coded H_3 GB tables) and by this file's general-n T-basis rule -- agreeing in all 6 slots. Mismatches: none

assertions.name: two_generic_h_samples_agree
assertions.source: h = 7/3 and h = 11/5: ranks [3, 21] vs [3, 21], distinct counts [9, 511] vs [9, 511]. A specialised rank is a LOWER bound on the symbolic one; two agreeing generic points is evidence, not a proof

assertions.name: h3_growth_is_linear_the_known_control
assertions.source: n = 3: 1 vertex available; distinct elements after k vertices = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9] = k+1 exactly -- the cyclic monoid of gammaGamma_threeStrand, recovered by a reducer that knows nothing about that theorem

assertions.name: h4_growth_is_free_the_collapse_does_not_generalise
assertions.source: n = 4: 2 vertices; distinct elements after k vertices = [1, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, 127, 255, 511] = 2^(k+1) - 1, i.e. every one of the 2^k words of length 2k is a DISTINCT element of H_4. The Hecke relations impose no collapse on the gamma-gamma submonoid up to k = 8

assertions.name: spans_are_proper_subspaces_at_both_n
assertions.source: n = 3: rank 3 of 6; n = 4: rank 21 of 24. Free growth and a proper span are consistent -- infinitely many distinct elements can live in a finite-dimensional subspace, and the constraint the route inherits is the SPAN, not the count

assertions.name: four_strand_span_is_absolutely_larger
assertions.source: span 3/6 = 1/2 at n = 3 against 21/24 = 7/8 at n = 4. Absolutely larger; the FRACTION is reported rather than asserted, since which of the two is the meaningful comparison is not established here

description: Does the three-strand gamma-gamma collapse generalise? Measures two things about the gamma-gamma submonoid at n = 3 and n = 4: how many DISTINCT elements the free monoid on the available vertices produces after the Hecke relations, and the rank of their linear span inside H_n. n = 3 is the control -- growth there must be linear, recovering gammaGamma_threeStrand from a reducer that knows nothing about it. Scope-(a): SIZE and SPAN only; no four-strand Markov trace is computed, so nothing is said about whether an H_4 gamma-gamma element reproduces an observable. The general-n reducer is validated against the corpus's hand-coded H_3 tables (CHECK 1).

data.method_caveat: growth and rank are measured with h specialised to a generic rational, so both are LOWER BOUNDS on the symbolic answer; reaching a maximum at a sample point therefore establishes it exactly, while a rank is 'at least r'. Two generic values agree (CHECK 2a)
what_this_does_not_measure: any four-strand Markov trace -- the Ocneanu recursion at n = 4 is not implemented here, so nothing is said about whether an H_4 gamma-gamma element reproduces an observable
growth beyond k = 8 vertices; 'free' is a measured statement about that range, not a proof
whether the H_4 span contains any element the corpus needs
